summary: Add an explicit DeepSeek Reference QA thinking control and compare disabled versus low on a frozen 20-question project and field-worker benchmark.
decision_refs: Thinking remains off by default and is sent only by QA V3 evidence decisions; extraction, vision, verification and legacy question routes are unchanged.
Provider reasoning text is neither placed in validated answer data nor persisted; ordinary provider usage, including reasoning token counters when returned, remains auditable.
Five out-of-project field questions intentionally have no supporting project evidence, so a safe non-answer or request for project-specific evidence/human review is the desired outcome.
Historical verification note: offline settings persistence and provider-scope rejection
Historical verification note: synthetic DeepSeek low-thinking request, usage accounting and private-reasoning exclusion
Historical verification note: legacy non-thinking policy regression
Historical verification note: frozen live 20-question disabled-versus-low comparison
Historical verification note: full Python, localization, spec, change and bundle gates
approval_evidence: The user explicitly requested testing of CoT on 20 questions and has already authorized the required API calls.
known_limitations: Provider-side thinking is not equivalent to exposing chain of thought and no reasoning text is retained for inspection.
One 20-question run measures this frozen Kapolei corpus and five synthetic out-of-project field scenarios; it does not establish construction-domain accuracy in general.
Assistant comparison against the answer key is not written as human adjudication and does not satisfy the fixed release gate by itself.
